[9:07:26 AM] 
 
>> Mayor Adler: Good morning. While we have folks that are taking their seats, we're going to go ahead 
and I'm going to call -- it's on. I'll move it up. All right. We're going to go ahead and call to order the 
special called meeting for the purposes of canvassing the recent election. There being the necessary 
quorum of the Austin city of Austin I call this meeting to order. It is Wednesday, may 18th, 9:00 in the 
morning. We're in the boards and commissions room, city hall, 301 west second street. Under state law 
only two councilmembers are necessary for a quorum to canvas an election. We have more than that. 
So I am declaring a quorum. We're now going to take up item number 1, to approve a resolution 
canvassing the results of the may 7th, 2016 special election held as a result of a valid initiative petition 
which gave voters the opportunity to vote for or against a proposed ordinance identified as proposition 
1. In this special election the returns of the election show that there were 39,109 votes for. And 49,208 
votes against proposition 1. Before I take a motion, is there anyone in the audience who would like to be 
heard on this matter? There being none, I'm going to entertain a motion on item number 1. Mayor pro 
tem? >> Tovo: I move that we approve the resolution canvassing and accepting the returns for the may 
7th, 2016 special election declaring proposition 1 not adopted. >> Mayor Adler: Is there a second to that 
motion? Mr. Renteria. There's been a motion by the  
 
[9:09:27 AM] 
 
mayor pro tem, seconded by councilmember Renteria. Is there any discussion? Seeing no discussion, 
we'll take a vote. Those in favor of this motion please say aye. Those opposed nay? It is unanimous on 
our dais, canvassing the votes with councilmembers kitchen and Zimmerman and Gallo and Casar not 
here. It passes. I am now going to adjourn the special called meeting and will at the same time call to 
order our budget session.
